description: Establishes an outbound TCP connection to a controlled lab listener, spawns cmd.exe locally, redirects the shell process standard input, output, and error streams, and relays command input and output over the established TCP socket. This creates an interactive reverse shell channel controlled by the remote listener.

reverse_shell_client.role: connects outbound to a controlled TCP listener, starts cmd.exe, redirects shell I/O streams, and relays interactive command traffic over the socket

tcp_listener.role: controlled lab listener that accepts the outbound TCP connection and provides interactive command input

shell_behavior.description: The sample connects to a remote TCP listener, starts cmd.exe with redirected standard streams, reads commands from the network stream, writes them into cmd.exe standard input, and sends command output and errors back to the listener asynchronously.
expected_actions: connect outbound to 192.168.67.5 on TCP port 8080
wrap network stream with StreamReader and StreamWriter
redirect standard input, output, and error
register asynchronous output and error event handlers
write received commands to cmd.exe standard input
send cmd.exe output back over TCP stream
terminate shell process if still running during cleanup
close stream resources when connection ends

code_placement: Reverse shell connection, child process creation, stream redirection, and interactive TCP relay logic are implemented directly inside the managed C# executable
execution_trigger: Program entry point starts the outbound TCP connection and launches the redirected shell after connection succeeds
execution_target: controlled TCP listener at 192.168.67.5:8080 and local cmd.exe child process

reverse_shell_client: StreamReader and StreamWriter wrapping socket stream
StandardInput.WriteLine used to pass commands to cmd.exe
StreamWriter.WriteLine used to return command output over TCP
absence of periodic beacon timing loop

network: outbound TCP connection from Windows VM to 192.168.67.5:8080
interactive command input received over established TCP stream
command output returned over the same TCP stream
no DNS beaconing is required if IP address is used directly
no HTTP or HTTPS traffic is required for this sample
process: A05_4_reverse_tcp_shell.exe runs as a standalone process
cmd.exe runs with no visible console window
parent process relays data between TCP socket and cmd.exe
child shell process may terminate when network connection closes
host: console output reports network sink connection failure if listener is unavailable
interactive commands such as whoami, hostname, cd, or echo return output to the listener
TCPView or netstat shows established connection to 192.168.67.5:8080
Sysmon or Procmon may record cmd.exe child process creation
Sysmon may record outbound network connection from the reverse shell executable

semantic_meaning: Demonstrates a controlled reverse TCP shell pattern in which a program initiates an outbound connection to a remote listener, spawns a local command interpreter, redirects the interpreter standard streams over the socket, and enables interactive operator-driven command execution through the established network channel.

control_notes.payload_effect: provides a controlled interactive cmd.exe shell over an outbound TCP connection for lab observation

success_conditions: controlled TCP listener is running on 192.168.67.5 port 8080
Windows VM can reach the listener over TCP
sample establishes outbound TCP connection to the listener
sample starts C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe as a child process
cmd.exe standard input, output, and error streams are redirected
commands entered from the listener are written to cmd.exe standard input
command output is returned to the listener over TCP
benign validation commands such as whoami, hostname, cd, or echo execute successfully
PCAP captures show interactive TCP traffic
Sysmon or Procmon records child process creation of cmd.exe
no secondary payload is downloaded or written to disk
connection cleanup terminates or closes shell resources
